text: The evening came all soft and violet-blue.
Sunny hopped along the garden edge of the bush.
She heard a busy rustling in the grass,
and little digging sounds among the roots.
A bandicoot, with soft and pointed nose,
was making tidy little holes to find his tea.
His round grey back was smooth as river stones,
his whiskers twitching gently as he worked.
“Hello,” said Sunny. “You're a busy one!”
“Almost done,” he said. “Then time for bed.”
He found one last sweet root and munched it slow,
then wiped his little nose upon the grass.
“A good day's digging makes a good night's sleep,”
he said, and gave a happy sleepy sigh.
So Sunny sighed a happy sigh as well,
and felt how good it was to end the day.
The bandicoot went pattering through the grass,
his little tracks like stitches in the dew.
He tucked himself into his grassy nest,
hidden warm and safe beneath the tussocks.
Sunny found a hollow soft with leaves,
and curled up cosy in the violet dark.
The bush was still. The dew lay on the grass.
Everything was peaceful, calm, and safe.
Her eyes grew heavy in the quiet night.
One slow blink… then another… then no more.
And Sunny slept not far from her new friend,
both of them dreaming of tomorrow's sun.
Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, busy bandicoot.
Goodnight, sleepy grass. Goodnight, little one.
